title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Sociology (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Sociology (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the pre-industrial cities?
options: Dependence on animate source of energy for the production of goods and services (hammers, pulleys, wheels)
Efficient methods of food preservation and storage.
High specialization of work like handicrafts work
The amount of surplus food has been limited by mechanized agriculture
questions.explanation: Pre-industrial cities relied on animate sources of energy for production.

questions.questionText: If the aim of the research is single-time description (political attitude at one time), which survey is most appropriate?
options: Cross-sectional Survey is the most appropriate
Trend and Cohort Studies are most appropriate
questions.explanation: A cross-sectional survey is designed for single-time descriptions.

questions.questionText: ____ is a system of authority, which is based on a rational calculation of advantages; i.e., it is based on rationally produced laws, norms and leaders are appointed or elected through legal procedures.
questions.explanation: In Weber's typology of authority, Rational-Legal Authority is based on a system of rules and procedures that are rationally established. Leaders derive their legitimacy from these established rules rather than from tradition or personal qualities. This type of authority is characteristic of modern bureaucratic states and organizations.

questions.questionText: Among the various levels of measurement, which one is appropriate to illustrate class categories as low, medium, and high?
questions.explanation: Ordinal levels of measurement are used for ranking categories.

questions.questionText: Virtual population analysis enables the scientist to predict the future catches.
questions.explanation: Modeling is used for predicting future outcomes in virtual population analysis.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is not the advantage of political sociology?
options: Political sociology tries to link politics with the general theories of society.
It studies power as distributed in some relationships in society, only embodied in the formal governmental structures
It allows the examination of the variety of structures and institutions that might otherwise be missed - politics in private organizations, in the family, in working places.
It tries to have a holistic approach.
questions.explanation: Political sociology examines power beyond just formal governmental structures.

questions.questionText: Economic aid has largely failed to promote modernization in developing countries because:
options: There are no clearly defined projects into which the money can be directed
The United Nations has refused to call on rich countries to provide it
Debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received
Rich countries are unwilling to provide sufficient aid
questions.explanation: High debt repayments with interest often exceed the original aid amount, creating a debt cycle that hinders development rather than promoting it. This is a key critique of international aid programs.

questions.questionText: According to the constructionist perspective, all of the following are sound expressions regarding the formation of ethnic identity except.
options: Ethnicity is acquired; it is not inborn.
questions.explanation: The constructionist perspective views ethnicity as socially constructed rather than biologically determined. It argues that ethnic identities are created, maintained, and modified through social interaction and historical processes, not innate or inherited traits. Therefore, describing ethnicity as 'an innate phenomenon' contradicts the constructionist view, which emphasizes ethnicity as learned, fluid, and contextual.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the basic assumptions in defining social problems Except
options: They have objective and subjective dimensions
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a basic assumption in defining social problems. The other three options correctly list key characteristics: harmful nature, social origins, and having both objective conditions and subjective perceptions.

questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect expression concerning social policy from the following.
options: Social policy has a linkage with nation-building.
Social policy is always a force for good.
Social policy aims at fostering community well-being.
questions.explanation: Social policy can have both positive and negative effects.

questions.questionText: A theoretical format that helps for a diagrammatic representation of social events is called ___
questions.explanation: Modeling provides a visual representation of social events.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the view of Karl Marx and Max Weber on the notion of social class?
options: They viewed social class as a source of social equality.
They both thought that the only factor influencing class formation was the economy.
They focused on the material aspect of the social class formation.
They viewed social class as a desirable social phenomenon.
questions.explanation: Marx and Weber focused on material conditions in class formation.

questions.questionText: Distinguish which of the following statements best describes the consequence of social problems?
options: Creation of job opportunities in reaction to the problems.
decline in mental health issues and disorders.
Strengthen social cohesion and social capital.
questions.explanation: Social problems often lead to disorganization and disintegration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the state of crime in Ethiopia?
options: Males are less criminal than females
Imprisonment is the most common type of punishment
Life imprisonment over-weights all other types of punishment
Capital punishment over-weights all other types of punishment
questions.explanation: Imprisonment is the prevalent form of punishment in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Terminal and ex-post evaluation is often conducted by ____________
questions.explanation: Ex-post evaluators assess outcomes after implementation.

questions.questionText: _______ is the study of the interactions between human and non-human nature in different cultures.
questions.explanation: Urban Ecology studies the interactions between humans and their environment.

questions.questionText: _______ Management is the process by which a product is sourced from an external supplier.
questions.explanation: Procurement management involves sourcing products externally.

questions.questionText: From the following, which one is False about Ceasar Lombroso's theory of born criminal?
options: Ancestral through back or hereditary as the main causes of crime
He compares the physical characteristics of criminals with Atavism, the early stage of human evolution
His theory gives attention to external factors like the environment shaping criminal behavior
He forwarded the argument that a born criminal has peculiar body characteristics that differ from normal people
questions.explanation: Lombroso's biological theory of criminality emphasized innate, biological factors rather than environmental influences. His theory of the 'born criminal' argued that criminals were evolutionary throwbacks (atavism) identifiable by physical anomalies. The statement claiming 'his theory gives attention to external factors like the environment' is incorrect because Lombroso specifically attributed criminal behavior to biological determinism, not environmental factors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct expression about the positive impact of globalization on national or ethnic identity?
options: Globalization has aggravated the role of national identity.
questions.explanation: Globalization can enhance cultural plurality.

questions.questionText: According to Weber _____ meant the probability that an event will be followed or accompanied by another event.
questions.explanation: Weber defined causality as the probability relationship between events. This concept was central to his methodology of understanding social phenomena through cause and effect relationships, while distinguishing between correlation and causation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a possible cause of social problems?
questions.explanation: Education is generally seen as a solution, not a cause of social problems.

questions.questionText: Urban sociology examines a great deal of issues except
options: History of urbanization to provide multiple perspectives
It does not emphasize on Physical aspects of urban contexts
The nature of and solutions to urban social problems
questions.explanation: Urban sociology does consider physical aspects of urban contexts.

questions.questionText: Identify the right sequence from the broadest to the narrowest in terms of their scope.
questions.explanation: Policies are broader than programs, which are broader than projects.

questions.questionText: ______ is a doctrine that assumes some groups always get the upper hand and rule the masses.
questions.explanation: Elitism refers to the idea that a small group holds power over the majority.

questions.questionText: ___________ the process through which religion's influence on other social institutions diminishes is:
questions.explanation: Secularization refers to the diminishing influence of religion.

questions.questionText: According to ____________ cities tended to grow in wedge-shaped patterns -- or sectors -- emanating from the central business district and centered on major transportation routes.
questions.explanation: The Sector Model describes urban growth in wedge-shaped patterns.

questions.questionText: The objective of crime measurement includes all except,
options: It is important to test, refine, and refute theories of crime causation
It enriches people's knowledge regarding attributes of crime and their current trend
It gives much attention to knowing trivial things to deal with crime and criminal behavior
It enables criminal justice agencies and other concerned bodies to plan for their future activities
questions.explanation: Crime measurement focuses on significant aspects, not trivialities.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is the central theme of the elite theory of political process?
options: The elite theory lays the conception that a society is divided into two groups and there are minorities or elite groups who rule the society and make decisions in a society.
The minority (the elite) is subordinate to the majority (the mass) because of its highly disorganized system of communication involving superior individuals.
The theory doesn't accept the existence of a single superior group, an elite group that monopolizes power in society.
It sees power as politically fragmented or diffused among the different sectors of society.
questions.explanation: The elite theory posits that a small group holds power over the majority.

questions.questionText: All of the following hold correct expressions of nationalism except.
options: It is an ideological movement aimed at maintaining the identity and unity of a nation.
It has something to do with state building and consolidation.
It may lead to the state collapse through bloody war.
Nationalism always remains ideological rather than appearing in the form of action.
questions.explanation: Nationalism can manifest in both ideology and action.

questions.questionText: _______ emphasis on the individual's interpretation of a situation and the importance of subjective meaning, was influential in the emergence of symbolic interactionism.
questions.explanation: Verstehen (German for 'understanding') is Weber's concept emphasizing the interpretive understanding of social action through empathically grasping the actor's subjective meanings. This approach, which focuses on how individuals interpret their social world, was influential in the development of symbolic interactionism, a perspective that examines how people create shared meanings through social interaction and interpretation of symbols.

questions.questionText: ___ argues that the logic and methods of the natural sciences are inappropriate in sociological theorizing and research because the subject matter of sociology is different from the subject matter of natural sciences.
questions.explanation: Interpretivism (also called anti-positivism) is an approach that argues that social sciences require different methods than natural sciences because human behavior involves meaning, intention, and interpretation. Unlike positivism, which advocates applying natural science methods to study society, interpretivism emphasizes understanding (verstehen) social action through the meanings actors attach to their behaviors rather than explaining causal relationships.

questions.questionText: All of the following are correct about primitive law Except:
options: It is the law of the pre-literate societies to resolve the daily problems of their members.
The law is handled not by religious persons or traditional shamans.
It is the law of the primitive societies before the emergence of the feudal system.
It is based on primitive cultural customs that are characterized by the lack of formal legal institutions or organization.
questions.explanation: In primitive law systems, legal matters were typically handled BY religious persons or traditional shamans, not separate from them. The statement that 'the law is handled not by religious persons or traditional shamans' is incorrect, as religious and traditional authorities were often central to primitive legal processes.

questions.questionText: Mr. X had governed Ethiopia for 35 years and the people highly believed that he would govern us again. The above descriptions qualify _____type of authority.
questions.explanation: Traditional authority is based on long-standing customs and beliefs.

questions.questionText: Anti-Apartheid Movement, Green Peace, Anti-Smoking Movement, and Anti-HIV Movement are an example of ______ groups.
questions.explanation: Promotional groups are social movements that actively advocate for specific causes or social changes rather than defending existing privileges or rights. These movements (Anti-Apartheid, Greenpeace, Anti-Smoking, Anti-HIV) all seek to promote particular social values, policies, or behavioral changes in society, distinguishing them from protective or defensive groups that primarily aim to preserve existing benefits or rights.

questions.questionText: _________ a stage in which people look for regularities or invariable social and natural laws through empirical research and theory.
questions.explanation: The Positive stage focuses on empirical research and laws.

questions.questionText: ____ refers to a kind of intellectual thinking in sociological theory that is distinct from contemporary sociological theory.
questions.explanation: Postmodern social theory represents a distinct approach that challenges the assumptions of modern sociological theory. It questions grand narratives, emphasizes plurality and diversity of perspectives, rejects universal truth claims, and focuses on deconstruction of traditional concepts.

questions.questionText: ______Plan provides a detailed description of the products (i.e., goods and services) to be procured from suppliers, the justification for procuring each product externally, and the schedule for procurement.
questions.explanation: A Procurement Plan outlines the details of sourcing products.

questions.questionText: Constitutional integrationist view of biological makeup as the main cause of crime includes all of the following factors, except.
questions.explanation: Gender is not typically viewed as a biological factor in this context.

questions.questionText: ___________ of a social problem comes from acknowledging that a particular social condition does negatively impact human lives.
questions.explanation: Objective reality refers to the acknowledgment of negative impacts.

questions.questionText: Systemic model examines the relationships between community attachment with all except
questions.explanation: The answer is 'None' because the systemic model of community attachment examines all of the other factors listed: length of residence, social position, and stage of life as determinants of community attachment.

questions.questionText: _______ are the overall results of project activities intended to achieve the immediate objectives.
questions.explanation: Outputs are the results of project activities.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the criteria applied in the policy formulation would then be measured in terms. Except
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a criterion used in policy formulation measurement. The other three options (Effectiveness, Efficiency, and Adequacy) are established criteria used to evaluate policy alternatives during formulation.

questions.questionText: ____ sees and understands social reality from the relationship between an individual's unique consciousness and the inter-subjective or shared consciousness that develops among people who share the same social world.
questions.explanation: Ethnomethodology, developed by Harold Garfinkel, examines how people make sense of their everyday social world through shared social practices. It focuses on the methods individuals use to construct their social reality and how common understandings emerge through interactions.

questions.questionText: Which phase of the policy-making process is marked by setting objectives?
questions.explanation: Policy formulation involves setting objectives.

questions.questionText: The process whereby the researcher specifies empirical observations that may be taken as indicators of the attributes contained within a given concept is called______________.
questions.explanation: Operationalization defines how concepts will be measured.

questions.questionText: Sociological theory, which argues that social problems arise from fundamental faults in the structure of a society and both reflect and reinforce inequalities based on social class, race, gender, and other dimensions, is called_____________.
questions.explanation: Conflict Theory focuses on structural inequalities.

questions.questionText: _________ are workers who sell their labor and who do not own their own means of production.
questions.explanation: Proletariats refer to the working class who sell their labor.

questions.questionText: ________ is best known in contemporary sociology for his contributions to our understanding of the patterns, or forms, of social interaction.
questions.explanation: Georg Simmel is recognized for his work on social interaction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is Not among Non-probability sampling methods?
questions.explanation: Random Sampling is a probability sampling method.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the essential features of the classical tradition except
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a feature of classical sociological tradition. The other three options correctly identify key characteristics of classical theory: grand narratives (comprehensive explanations), universal assumptions, and focus on social change theories.

questions.questionText: ______ is defined as a method in philosophy that begins with the individual and his own conscious experience and tries to avoid prior assumptions, prejudices, and philosophical dogmas.
questions.explanation: Phenomenology, associated with Edmund Husserl and Alfred Schutz in sociology, is a philosophical approach that examines subjective experience by setting aside preconceptions to understand phenomena as they appear to consciousness. It focuses on how individuals perceive and make sense of their lived experiences.

questions.questionText: Erving Goffman celebrated study of behavior in a mental asylum, Asylums: Essays on the Social Situation of Mental Patients and Other Inmates in 1961 was the best example of ______ research in sociology.
questions.explanation: Goffman's work is a classic example of field research.

questions.questionText: _______ denotes those issues on which the government and its institutions feel compelled to act (e.g., the approval of treaties, or government departmental budget requests).
questions.explanation: The governmental agenda includes issues requiring government action.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the features of monitoring except?
questions.explanation: The option 'C&B' (Cost & Benefit) is not a standard feature of monitoring. Monitoring typically involves assessing intermediate results, attributes/indicators, and multi-level results throughout a project's implementation, but cost-benefit analysis is typically part of evaluation rather than monitoring.

questions.questionText: ______ is the international transfer of capital, goods, or services from a country or international organization for the benefit of the recipient country or its population.
questions.explanation: Foreign Aid refers to international assistance for development.

questions.questionText: _____ considered the law as an ideology of the ruling class that conceals the existing class division and inequality in society and exploitation of the labor class.
questions.explanation: Karl Marx viewed law as a tool of the ruling class.

questions.questionText: The best-known sociologist as a micro-sociologist who played a significant role in the development of small-group research is
questions.explanation: Georg Simmel is renowned for his pioneering work in micro-sociology, focusing on the forms and patterns of small-group interactions and social relationships. Unlike Marx, Weber, and Comte who primarily analyzed macro-level social structures and historical processes, Simmel examined dyads, triads, and small group dynamics, making fundamental contributions to understanding social interactions at the micro level.

questions.questionText: When researchers define the notion of self-esteem as positive or negative feelings towards oneself, it is called_______________.
questions.explanation: Operationalization defines how self-esteem is measured.

questions.questionText: ______ is a systematic evaluation of how effectively a policy addresses the targeted problem or issue, meets people's needs, and achieves its goals.
questions.explanation: Policy analysis evaluates the effectiveness of policies.

questions.questionText: It is extremely difficult to gather reliable statistics pertaining to the types, distribution, and frequency of crime and delinquency, because:
options: Most criminals fail to be discovered
Victims might be at criminal cases
questions.explanation: All listed factors contribute to the difficulty in gathering reliable crime statistics.

questions.questionText: Our_________ position is directly underpinning our theoretical perspective.
questions.explanation: Epistemological positions influence theoretical perspectives.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true According to Differential Associations theory
options: Criminality is a normally learned behavior
The one who lives with a thief has a high probability of becoming a thief
Biological traits and drives play a crucial role in shaping human behavior
Criminal behavior is learned in interaction with other persons
questions.explanation: According to Sutherland's Differential Association theory, criminal behavior is learned through social interaction rather than being determined by biological factors. The theory specifically rejects biological determinism, emphasizing that criminal behavior is learned just like any other behavior through social processes and interactions.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is not the major concern area of the sociology of law:
options: Analyses of the social role of the criminal, lawyer, judge, and it did not relate to the general structure of the society.
The sociology of law is primarily concerned with how the formal norms of society (legal practices) and enforcing agents act towards each other and deviants and criminals.
Sociology of law has no relationship with political sociology a concern for the nature of legitimate authority and social control.
The sociology of law studies the laws governing the development of human society and the effects of legal provisions.
questions.explanation: The sociology of law does analyze the social roles of legal actors (criminals, lawyers, judges) AND relates these to the general structure of society. The statement claiming it 'did not relate to the general structure of society' is incorrect, as connecting legal institutions to broader social structures is a central concern of the sociology of law.

questions.questionText: All of the following are among the Factors to be taken into account in Planning. Except
options: Values, Interests, Beliefs, Ethics, and Slants (VIBES)
questions.explanation: Adoption of the plan is not a factor in planning.

questions.questionText: A design that studies the same people, events or activities over a time period is called_____________.
questions.explanation: Longitudinal studies track the same subjects over time.

questions.questionText: ____ asks if, is the project both advantageous and acceptable to the people affected by it.
questions.explanation: Social feasibility assesses the acceptability of a project.

questions.questionText: The capitalist world economy is what Wallerstein(1974) would call a 'world system'. This term refers to:
options: means of transporting money between different areas of a country
An empire with a bureaucratic administration but no political center
An awareness of risks and dangers that affect the environment as a whole
unit with a division of labor that extends across ethnic and cultural groups
questions.explanation: In Wallerstein's World-Systems Theory, a 'world system' refers to an integrated economic unit with a global division of labor that transcends political and cultural boundaries. It includes core, semi-peripheral and peripheral regions with different economic functions and power relations.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is different from the others?
questions.explanation: The option 'Has general objectives' is less specific than the others.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the distinguishing features of terminal evaluation except?
options: It undertakes a careful examination of performance
It takes a longer time to review the initial outputs and effects
questions.explanation: Terminal evaluation focuses on final outcomes, not intermediate results.

questions.questionText: Increases in real GNP per capita occur when
options: Government programs direct resources away from investment goods to consumer goods.
Tariffs and quotas prevent countries from trading and thus prevent dollars from leaving each country.
The rate of growth in real GNP is greater than the rate of growth in the population.
The level of consumption expenditures rises relative to the level of saving.
questions.explanation: Increases in real GNP per capita occur when economic growth outpaces population growth.

questions.questionText: ______ is the spread of worldwide practices, relations, consciousness, and organization of social life.
questions.explanation: Globalization refers to the interconnectedness of social practices and relations.

questions.questionText: ______ is the study of legal institutions of the society in light of sociological concepts, theories, and approaches.
questions.explanation: Sociology of law examines legal institutions through sociological lenses.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the factors for the coming of the welfare state and social policy EXCEPT
questions.explanation: The answer is 'None' because advancing industrialism, labor movements, and capitalist development are all recognized factors that contributed to the emergence of welfare states and social policies. The option 'None' is not a factor in this development.

questions.questionText: According to Durkheim Organic solidarity is
options: It is the characteristic of primitive society
Largely dominate common belief and custom
questions.explanation: Durkheim's concept of organic solidarity refers to social cohesion based on high social differentiation and interdependence created by division of labor in complex modern societies. Unlike mechanical solidarity (found in simpler societies), organic solidarity results from differences between individuals and their complementary functions.

questions.questionText: _____ is performed by persons who have a direct role in the program/project or mid-term evaluation can be done by the management team persons assigned from the implementing agency.
questions.explanation: Mid-term evaluation is conducted by those directly involved in the project.

questions.questionText: __________ assumes that effective social policy is built on the cornerstone of careful problem definition.
questions.explanation: The problem-centered approach emphasizes defining issues clearly.

questions.questionText: Classical criminology differs from positive criminology in that, classical criminology:
options: Emphasized on the criminal not the crime
Emphasized the actor not the action
Insisted punishment should fit the criminal
Emphasized on the crime not the criminal
questions.explanation: Classical criminology, associated with Cesare Beccaria and Jeremy Bentham, focused on the crime rather than the criminal, emphasizing free will, rational choice, and proportional punishment. In contrast, positive criminology (developed by Lombroso and others) focused on the criminal, viewing crime as determined by biological, psychological, or social factors beyond individual control. Classical criminology advocated that punishment should fit the crime, not be tailored to the criminal.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a characteristic of urban urbanization
options: The urban community is a complex multi-group society.
Formal means of social control dominate such as law, legislation, police, and court
It is dominated by primary relations.
Urban society is heterogeneous and known for its diversity and complexity.
questions.explanation: Urban areas are characterized by secondary (formal, impersonal, specialized) rather than primary relations (intimate, personal, face-to-face). While rural communities typically feature strong primary relations and personal connections, urban environments are marked by more impersonal, contractual, and specialized relationships. This distinction was notably emphasized by sociologists like Tönnies (Gemeinschaft vs. Gesellschaft) and Durkheim (mechanical vs. organic solidarity).

questions.questionText: _____ is an initial review of project ideas and concepts to see if they should be advanced or abandoned at an early stage.
questions.explanation: Screening assesses project ideas for viability.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the requirements for studying social problems Except?
options: Evaluating the social norms and values
questions.explanation: Evaluating social norms and values is not a requirement for studying social problems.

questions.questionText: Delinquency differs from other forms of crime in that, delinquency is:
options: breach of minor laws by the young
Any offense against human life and property
Any offense against minor laws by an organized group of citizens
Any offense against conventional laws by youngsters
questions.explanation: Delinquency specifically refers to offenses committed by minors.

questions.questionText: __________ is seen as the process of change towards those types of social, economic, and political systems that have developed in Western Europe and North America.
questions.explanation: Modernization Theory views development as a linear process through which traditional societies progress toward becoming modern societies resembling Western industrialized nations. It emphasizes industrialization, urbanization, rationalization, and democratization as key processes, suggesting all societies follow similar paths of development.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false about urbanization?
options: One necessary condition for urbanization was surplus products
Population growth is the only reason for urbanization.
The advancement of agricultural technology is a factor of urbanization.
questions.explanation: Population growth is not the only reason for urbanization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is or are NOT among the Advantages of the Field-research Method?
options: It is the only method available when the researcher studies an unknown group to outsiders.
Field research provides much richer information about social life.
Field research gives the investigator more flexibility than other methods.
Different researchers can come up with differing descriptions of the same phenomenon.
questions.explanation: The challenge of different researchers potentially coming up with differing descriptions of the same phenomenon is actually a limitation of field research, not an advantage. This issue relates to concerns about reliability and researcher subjectivity in qualitative field research methods.

questions.questionText: According to Parsons, the relationship between two or more individuals who work with certain orientations or goals is known as_______
questions.explanation: Social action refers to interactions with shared goals.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following scholars defined religion in terms of a distinction between the sacred and the profane?
questions.explanation: Emile Durkheim, in his seminal work 'The Elementary Forms of Religious Life' (1912), defined religion based on the fundamental distinction between sacred and profane elements. For Durkheim, religion is a unified system of beliefs and practices related to sacred things - things set apart and forbidden - that unite adherents into a moral community or church. This sacred-profane dichotomy is the cornerstone of his sociological approach to religion.

questions.questionText: Which statement depicts the best definition of sustainable development?
options: It means optimal utilization of natural resources.
Sustainable use of natural resources without considering the needs of the future generation.
The present generation fulfills its needs while considering the needs of the future generation as well.
questions.explanation: Sustainable development balances current and future needs.

questions.questionText: Choose the WRONG statement regarding participant observation.
options: Participant observation can involve an array of data collection methods.
All participant observation is fieldwork and the reverse is also true.
Participant observation uses data collection methods like sampling.
Participant observation employs interviews, unobtrusive and checklist methods.
questions.explanation: The statement 'All participant observation is fieldwork and the reverse is also true' is incorrect. While participant observation is a form of fieldwork, not all fieldwork involves participant observation. Fieldwork can include non-participatory methods such as naturalistic observation, structured observation, or other data collection techniques where the researcher doesn't actively participate in the setting being studied.

questions.questionText: Select the best statement that explains social problems.
options: Social problems are integral to our daily lives.
All social problems acquire a perennial quality.
Social problems are never associated with us.
Social problems always have positive consequences.
questions.explanation: Social problems affect everyone in society.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a feature of globalization?
options: An increasing awareness of the world as a whole
The destruction of distance through communications technologies
The stretching of social relations beyond national boundaries
questions.explanation: Globalization is typically characterized by a reduction in the power of nation-states, not their extension, as transnational corporations, international organizations, and global movements increasingly challenge state sovereignty. The other options correctly identify features of globalization.

questions.questionText: In_____ view modernity was defined by its organic solidarity and the weakening of the collective conscience.
questions.explanation: Durkheim emphasized organic solidarity in modernity.

questions.questionText: A. Associated with entertainment or leisure B. Indicate relationship C. Synonym of economic D. Opposite of individual
questions.explanation: This question appears to be asking about the meaning of 'social'. The correct answer is D because 'social' is the opposite of 'individual', referring to collective or group aspects of human life rather than individual aspects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about political sociology?
options: It studies the origin and development of political ideas
Political sociology describes the formal structure and functioning of the government
Traditionally the discipline is concerned with the study of the state, the government, and public administration.
It examines the link between politics and society and analyses the relationship between social structure and political structure, and social behavior and political behavior in society.
questions.explanation: Political sociology focuses on the interplay between politics and society.

questions.questionText: When the aim or the main purpose of the study is to discover the distribution of certain traits or attributes, we call it_________________ survey.
questions.explanation: Descriptive surveys aim to discover distributions of traits.

questions.questionText: ______ is money that produces more money, but Marx tells us it is more than that: it is also a particular social relation.
questions.explanation: Capital refers to money used to generate more wealth.

questions.questionText: ________ is research that usually emphasizes words and meanings rather than numbers and percentages, while _________ is research that usually emphasizes numbers, percentages, and measurement in the collection and analysis of data, respectively.
questions.explanation: Qualitative research focuses on in-depth understanding of social phenomena through words, meanings, and interpretations, using methods like interviews, observation, and textual analysis. Quantitative research, conversely, emphasizes numerical data, statistical analysis, and measurement, using methods like surveys, experiments, and structured observation. These represent different methodological approaches to studying social reality, each with its own strengths and limitations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about development?
options: The meaning of development has changed over a period of time in terms of its approaches, strategies, and paradigms.
In the 1950s and 1960s, development emphasized the level of economic growth, measured from economic indices such as per capita GNP.
Development is not purely an economic phenomenon but rather a multi-dimensional process.
questions.explanation: All statements reflect the evolving understanding of development.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not correct about world system theory?
options: World economy, integrated through the market rather than a political center
It is a 'multicultural territorial division of labor in which the production and exchange of basic goods and raw materials is necessary for the everyday life of its inhabitants.'
It says, if you want to develop, be like us (the West). Development follows essentially the same pattern in all societies.
Among the most important structures of the current world system is a power hierarchy between the core and periphery.
questions.explanation: World system theory recognizes diverse paths to development, not a single model.

questions.questionText: _______ is the process by which social values are internalized by societal members.
questions.explanation: Socialization is the process of internalizing societal values.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of social problems?
options: They have objective and subjective dimensions
They are always recognized by society
questions.explanation: Not all social problems are universally recognized by society.
